page: Microsoft Azure F2amds_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by a 4.5 GHz AMD EPYC 9V45 processor using the x86_64 architecture. The server provides 2 dedicated physical cores without hyperthreading and is equipped with 16.0 GB of RAM, yielding an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio. High-speed local ephemeral storage is bundled via a 236 GB local NVMe SSD. The processor includes 32 MB of L3 cache, along with vector extensions including AVX-512, AVX-VNNI, and SHA cryptographic extensions.

Benchmark testing reveals exceptional single-core compute capabilities. The instance achieved top-tier performance in single-core stress-ng tests (3,755.98), Geekbench single-core testing (2,855.0), and single-threaded gzip compression (40.8 GB/sec). However, due to its low core count of two vCPUs, multi-core throughput and parallel compute workloads rank in the average to weak tiers, such as software compilation with Clang and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. Read memory bandwidth on uncached blocks is recorded at 47.98 GB/sec, while Redis SET performance reaches 6.09 million operations per second.

The F2amds_v7 instance offers high memory density and fast per-core instruction execution, making it qualitatively cost-effective for single-threaded processing and small-footprint memory-bound tasks. The local NVMe storage provides rapid scratch space access for memory-heavy operations, though overall scaling is constrained by the limited core count. Optimal workloads include in-memory caching, single-threaded data processing, lightweight database engines, and memory-intensive microservices requiring high clock speeds.
description: Microsoft Azure F2amds_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine featuring two dedicated physical cores powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked at 4.5 GHz. Built on x86_64 architecture, the instance provides 16.0 GB of system memory, delivering an 8.0 GB per core allocation, alongside a local 236 GB NVMe SSD for fast storage access. Single-core performance benchmarks place this server in the top tier, backed by robust results in single-threaded decompression, text processing, and single-core synthetic CPU scores. Conversely, parallel execution tasks such as software compilation and multi-threaded file extraction are limited by the two-core ceiling, yielding average to lower-tier multi-threaded benchmark results. Qualitative resource density remains strong for low-core memory-intensive applications. F2amds_v7 is well suited for running lightweight database servers, in-memory key-value stores like Redis, single-core analytical tasks, and microservices requiring high memory density relative to vCPU capacity.
